title: EnQode: Fast Amplitude Embedding for Quantum Machine Learning Using Classical Data
problem: Conventional amplitude embedding (AE) for QML requires deep variable-length circuits with extensive gate usage, causing high output error and noise-driven inconsistencies that degrade model accuracy across samples.
motivation: Quantum machine learning on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices requires efficient, low-depth amplitude encoding to minimize cumulative gate error and achieve model robustness.
method: Instead of building a unique circuit for each data sample, EnQode groups similar samples and creates a single circuit template—an ansatz—that represents each group's average state. This ansatz is designed to be shallow (short) and tailored to the specific quantum hardware, minimizing the number of quantum gates. Since all samples in a group share the same circuit, noise from quantum hardware imperfections stays consistent rather than varying unpredictably per sample. This consistency, combined with reduced gates, ensures reliable learning on noisy quantum computers.
key_novelty: Amplitude embedding that clusters samples symbolically, then standardizes circuit depth while minimizing gates to ensure consistent noise levels on NISQ devices.
contributions: Sample clustering to derive cluster mean states
Standardized circuit depth reducing noise variance across samples
Over 94% fidelity in data mapping on NISQ devices
primary_theme: Noise-resilient amplitude embedding for NISQ devices via symbolic clustering
